newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: OAU allows other Africans to seek UN top post.
newsitem.headline: OAU allows other Africans to seek UN top post.

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity has opened the way for another African to be elected secretary-general of the United Nations by urging African leaders to submit names other than Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

The move by President Paul Biya of Cameroon, the OAU chairman, appeared to break a deadlock following the November 19 veto by the United States when African states still seemed reluctant to put forward other candidates while Boutros-Ghali remained in play.

"It emerges from my numerous contacts and the consultations I have made that, in order to preserve Africa's chances for a second five-year term of office, it is time for African States who do so wish to present other quality candidates, together with that of Dr Boutros Boutros-Ghali," Biya, said in a letter to African leaders, obtained by Reuters on Monday.
"These states may refer directly to the Security Council and inform the current Chairman of the OAU," Biya said in his letter, dated November 29.
"In view of the degree of urgency conferred to this issue, I would be most grateful if you could let me know your opinion at your earliest convenience," he said.
The OAU, at its summit in Yaounde, Cameroon, last July backed Boutros-Ghali for another five years in office.

The current president of the U.N. Security Council, Francesco Paulo Fulci of Italy, is expected to call a meeting on the issue Wednesday afternoon. Diplomats said they expected at least one African candidate, to be nominated by then.
"And by Friday the floodgates should be opening," said a senior African envoy.

Boutros-Ghali's term expires Dec. 31 and the United States has vowed to keep using its veto if necessary to deny him a second term on the grounds that the United Nations needs new leadership to carry out reforms.

Boutros-Ghali's immediate predecessors -- Javier Perez de Cuellar of Peru, Kurt Waldheim of Austria and U Thant of Burma -- all had two five-year terms and this has become an unwritten U.N. tradition.
A number of African diplomats have been mentioned as possible candidates but none has been formally submitted yet.
As recently as a week ago, Ambassador Legwaila Joseph Legwail of Botswana, a Security Council member, told reporters: "We don't have any (new) list. It is composed of one person, Dr. Boutros-Ghali."

Among Africans spoken of as potential candidates are: Under-Secretary-General Kofi Annan of Ghana, who heads U.N. peacekeeping operations; Ivory Coast Foreign Minister Amara Essy; Hamid Algabid of Niger, secretary-general of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference; OAU secretary-general Salim A. Salim of Tanzania; Foreign Minister Moustapha Niasse of Senegal, and Olara Otunnu, a former Ugandan U.N. envoy who heads the New York-based International Peace Academy.
More names may emerge after a French-led summit in Ougadougou, the capital of Burkina Faso, on Thursday.
